subject: Banking
title: The Interchange Fee Machine
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Interchange Fee Machine.

hook.text: Every card swipe costs the merchant 1.5-3.5% in fees. On $5 trillion in US card volume.

buildup.text: Interchange fees flow from the merchant's bank to the cardholder's bank. The card network takes a small cut too.

discovery.text: Your bank uses interchange revenue to fund rewards. Your cashback and airline miles are paid by merchants.

twist.text: Small businesses pay the same rates as large chains but can't negotiate. Interchange hits independent shops hardest.

climax.text: Card rewards are a wealth transfer. Merchants pay fees, card users get perks. Cash users subsidize everyone.

punchline.text: $160 billion in swipe fees. Merchants fund your airline miles.

quiz.question: Who ultimately pays for credit card rewards programs?
